articles.excerpt: Disclosure: this post was written with an AI assistant, working from the project's code and docs. I run ultraielts, a free site where people preparing for IELTS take full mock tests in the computer-de…
articles.body: Disclosure: this post was written with an AI assistant, working from the project's code and docs. I run ultraielts , a free site where people preparing for IELTS take full mock tests in the computer-delivered format. The interface is in Turkish because that's who it's for. The tests are in English, as on the real exam. The worst bug a practice test can have isn't a crash. It's a question with two defensible answers, or an answer key that's simply wrong. A student marks NOT GIVEN, the key says FALSE, and from then on they stop trusting every score the site gives them. The tests on the site are original (written for it, no third-party material), and a pipeline helps write them, so I needed a check that is stricter than me rereading the key at 2 a.m.

articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 3: Slow and Steady . Demo https://youtu.be/7FTC_TPzTn8 The video shows the setup guide, a fictional appointment notice, and the explanation produced by PlainSpeak. Code PlainSpeak on GitHub How I Built It PlainSpeak is a browser app that uses the open-weight Gemma 3:1B model through Ollama running locally.

articles.title: Most App Store Rejections Are Not About Your Code
articles.excerpt: Every engineer I know has the same first reaction to an App Store rejection: open the crash logs. That is almost always the wrong place to look. In my experience the build is fine. What failed is ever…
articles.body: Every engineer I know has the same first reaction to an App Store rejection: open the crash logs. That is almost always the wrong place to look. In my experience the build is fine. What failed is everything around the build: a login the reviewer could not get past, a form you filled in from memory, a calendar rule nobody on the team knew existed. I managed App Store and Play Console releases as CTO at RAQTS, across mobile apps and a Unity platform, and I have been on the wrong end of enough review threads to stop treating store review as a final hurdle. Now I treat it like any other external system with an undocumented contract: probe it early, on purpose, and keep a checklist of the ways it fails.

articles.body: Originally published at tensorust.com . Short answer: Curators feature numbers they can quote, not opinions. articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 23, 2007: NASA launches Harmony module to ISS on STS-120 space shuttle mission
articles.excerpt: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On October 23, 2007, the space shuttle Discovery launched the Harmony module to the International Space Station . The Harmony module is a utility hub 14 feet wide and 24 feet long, or about the length of a minibus. It joins the European Space Agency's Columbus module and Japan's Kibo laboratory and serves as the crew quarters for the American astronauts. Once it was installed, the space station grew from about the size of a three-bedroom house to something more like a five-bedroom house. When astronauts delivered Harmony to the space station , they left it temporarily attached to the Unity node. After the shuttle left, astronauts used the space station's robotic arm to move the shuttle docking port out of the way at the Destiny module.

articles.title: RS-25 Engine Tests at NASA Stennis
articles.excerpt: Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the sam…
articles.body: NASA/Danny Nowlin Teams at NASA’s Stennis Space Center near Bay St. Louis, Mississippi tested RS-25 engine No. 10001 on Oct. 21, 2026. The hot fire test lasted for almost eight-and-a-half minutes (500 seconds), the same amount of time RS-25 engines fire during launch of NASA’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, with a 111% power level. For each Artemis mission, four RS-25 engines produce up to 2 million pounds of combined thrust to help launch the SLS rocket. Prior to use, all RS-25 engines are proven flightworthy at NASA Stennis. While this developmental engine will not be used in flight, the hot fire test provides NASA and NASA’s prime engine contractor L3Harris Technologies with the capability to capture critical data to improve engine performance and reliability.

(Image credit: Tim McCollum) Astrophotographer Tim McCollum captured a spectacular view of Orionid meteors sharing the night sky with a host of deep sky wonders on Oct. 21, as the annual shooting star display ramped up to peak activity. Comet 1P/Halley may be over 3 billion miles (4.8 kilometers) from Earth , but that didn't stop it from putting on a breathtaking display earlier this week, as particles cast off by the ancient wanderer carved a fiery path through the autumn sky. articles.body: 3 min read Preparations for Next Moonwalk Simulations Underway (and Underwater) NASA is helping to foster long-term energy security in Virginia.  NASA’s Langley Research Center in Hampton, Virginia, is partnering with the Virginia Department of Energy to support informed decisions for effective energy generation, delivery and use by providing solar, meteorological, and future weather risk datasets for energy system modeling and planning purposes. Under a new Space Act Agreement announced during a ceremony Friday, the partnership will use NASA expertise in atmospheric sciences to assist Virginia Energy in support of resiliency studies, resource analysis, and long-term energy planning.

articles.body: Last week, Starshield - the version of SpaceX's Starlink used by the Ukrainian military - was throttled to block terminals traveling above certain speeds from accessing the service. The Ukrainian army's interceptors, which counter Russian drones carrying bombs, suddenly stopped working at high speeds, making it easier for Russia to attack the country's energy infrastructure and leading to a reported two deaths and at least 17 injuries . The Ukrainian military reported receiving no advance warning about the Starshield speed restriction. articles.title: Never finishing the fight: Where did Xbox go wrong with Halo?
articles.excerpt: After a failed soft reboot and a remake of the original, the Halo universe is facing yet another major creative shift. But has Xbox learned any lessons this time?
articles.body: Halo: Campaign Evolved was Xbox’s second attempt at refreshing the 2001 sci-fi FPS classic, and it is perfectly fine. A cromulent remake, if ever there was one, but it’s hardly a franchise-saver, especially as Xbox looks to rethink its studio structure and approach to renowned IPs like Halo or Gears of War . Halo hasn’t been the same since original developer Bungie — now owned by Sony and working on Destiny and Marathon — departed, leaving 343 Industries (now Halo Studios) to guide the franchise. Neither Halo 4 nor 5 meaningfully evolved the gameplay formula or overarching narrative. Halo Infinite found more success by reheating what “old Halo felt like” and sticking it into a half-baked open world, but it still felt far from the series’ glory days.
